cards.b: V followed by I; sounds final.
Ends on chord V; sounds unfinished.
V followed by vi; a surprise instead of I.
Chord V with a minor 7th added, e.g. G B D F in C major.
Four notes in stacked minor 3rds; tense and unstable.
A note held over into the next chord that clashes, then falls by step to resolve.
A long held tonic note in the bass while the chords above change.
A held 5th degree in the bass; builds tension, often before a return.
Uses only notes of the key.
Uses notes outside the key; colourful, typical of Romantic music.
A change of key within a piece.
G major (dominant), F major (subdominant), A minor (relative minor).
Same tonic but the mode changes, e.g. C major to C minor.

gaps.s: A perfect cadence is chord V followed by chord ___.
An interrupted cadence goes from V to ___.
An imperfect cadence ends on chord ___.
A change of key is called a ___.
The key a fifth above the tonic is the ___ key.
A held bass note on the 5th degree is a ___ pedal.
Harmony using notes outside the key is ___.
A note held over that clashes with a new chord is a ___.

short.q: Describe the sound and effect of an interrupted cadence.
short.model: It moves V to vi; the listener expects the final chord I but hears vi, so it sounds like a surprise and the phrase continues.

short.q: How can you recognise a modulation to the dominant from the notation?
short.model: A new sharp (raised 7th of the old key) appears, and a perfect cadence confirms the new key.

short.q: Name the chords I, IV and V in C major.
short.model: C major, F major and G major.

short.q: Why is a dominant pedal effective in the Baroque or Classical music?
short.model: It holds the dominant note, building tension that is released when the tonic returns.

short.q: Explain the difference between consonant and dissonant harmony.
short.model: Consonant harmony sounds stable and at rest; dissonant harmony sounds tense and needs to resolve.
